ACID Properties.title: ACID — Wikipedia
ACID Properties.snippet: In computer science, ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability) is a set of properties of database transactions intended to guarantee data validity despite errors, power failures, and other mishaps.

ACID Properties.title: Transactions — PostgreSQL Documentation
ACID Properties.snippet: PostgreSQL transactions adhere to the ACID model. Atomic commits and durable writes are guaranteed through the Write-Ahead Log (WAL).

ACID Properties.title: What does ACID actually mean in databases?
ACID Properties.snippet: Top answer: ACID = Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency (valid state transitions), Isolation (concurrent txn safety), Durability (survives crashes).

ACID Properties.title: Database System Concepts (Silberschatz, Korth, Sudarshan)
ACID Properties.snippet: ACID properties guarantee that database transactions are processed reliably and preserve data integrity under concurrent access and failures.

Dijkstra's Algorithm.title: Dijkstra's algorithm — Wikipedia
Dijkstra's Algorithm.snippet: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths from a source vertex in a graph with non-negative edge weights. With a binary heap it runs in O((V+E) log V).

Dijkstra's Algorithm.title: Introduction to Algorithms (CLRS) — Chapter 24
Dijkstra's Algorithm.snippet: Dijkstra's algorithm solves the single-source shortest-paths problem on a weighted, directed graph with non-negative edge weights.

Dijkstra's Algorithm.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm — Stanford CS161 Lecture Notes
Dijkstra's Algorithm.snippet: The algorithm requires non-negative edge weights. For graphs containing negative weights, Bellman-Ford must be used instead.

Dijkstra's Algorithm.title: Why does Dijkstra's algorithm fail on negative weights?
Dijkstra's Algorithm.snippet: Accepted answer: Dijkstra's greedy choice assumes that once a vertex is finalized its distance cannot decrease — negative edges break this invariant.

Dijkstra's Algorithm.title: Shortest Paths — Princeton Algorithms (algs4)
Dijkstra's Algorithm.snippet: Using a Fibonacci heap, Dijkstra runs in O(E + V log V); with a binary heap, O((V+E) log V). It is not dynamic programming — it is a greedy algorithm.

Big-O Notation.title: Big O notation — Wikipedia
Big-O Notation.snippet: Big O notation describes the limiting behavior of a function when the argument tends towards a particular value or infinity — an asymptotic upper bound.

Big-O Notation.title: Algorithm complexity — MDN Web Docs Glossary
Big-O Notation.snippet: Big-O notation expresses the worst-case growth rate of an algorithm's running time as input size increases.

Big-O Notation.title: Asymptotic Analysis — CLRS Chapter 3
Big-O Notation.snippet: Big-O describes an asymptotic upper bound on the growth rate of a function — it is not a tight bound (that is Θ).

Big-O Notation.title: What is a plain English explanation of Big-O?
Big-O Notation.snippet: Most upvoted answer of all time: Big-O tells you how the runtime grows relative to input size, ignoring constants and lower-order terms.
